Triage — first-touch grading (concentrated round, triage seat, session `session_0138jAR5jeREBpm4dhVvbWY7`): **promoted to `pm:queue`, type Task, `domain:metadata`.**

Concrete, user-visible on any zh session of the showcase app, with named file surfaces (`examples/app-showcase/src/system/translations/index.ts` + `src/ui/apps/index.ts`). Graded Task rather than Bug: the bundle's own declared coverage claim is columns/fields ("EVERY field surfaced as a column"), and nav labels sit outside that declaration — nothing declared is violated, the coverage is simply incomplete. Routed `domain:metadata` because the exercised subsystem is the platform translation-bundle machinery over app/navigation metadata (examples land with the subsystem they exercise). Dispatch note (premise-first): repro is pinned to a 08-17 SHA — re-check the bundle on current `main` before dispatch; if a nav-translation mechanism landed since, the card may be partially delivered. Not a release blocker (example-app locale completeness).

Container & model: `S–M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` — no path-derived tier mandate. ⚠️ Held at default rather than the `sonnet` floor **deliberately**: this looks mechanical but is not gate-decided. No gate can tell a *complete* nav-label bundle from a *partial* one, and the key-naming convention has to match the bundle's existing scheme rather than invent a second one. The floor is for cards whose correctness the gate farm settles; this one's is settled by judgement.
Clause-②: no — example-app translation data. No acceptance face, no public surface, no `packages/spec/**`.
Serial constraints cleared: `domain:metadata` in flight is **#9327** only (this round's sibling), landing in the `packages/metadata*` reference-traversal family — **different package, zero overlap**. Nothing else in any lane declares `examples/app-showcase/**`.

## Premise, and what makes it more than a typo fix

The card measures a **mixed-locale shell** on a zh-CN session: view tabs, list columns, field labels and option values render Chinese (covered by `ShowcaseTranslationBundle`), while the **left sidebar app navigation** stays English throughout — `Capability Map`, `Page Authoring`, `Workspace`, `My Work`, `Approvals`, `New Project (Wizard)`, `Settings`, … — because the bundle contains **no app/navigation keys at all** in either locale block, so the sidebar has nothing to fall back on but its English source labels.

⭐ The bundle's own header states it covers *"EVERY field surfaced as a column"* and enforces *"a list never mixes locales"*. The nav labels sit outside that stated remit, which is exactly why nothing caught it — **the invariant was scoped narrower than the surface it reads as covering.** Worth a word in the report on whether the remit sentence should widen with the fix, so the same gap does not reopen for the next un-covered surface.

## PM mechanism assumptions — measure, falsification welcome

1. **The label set lives in `examples/app-showcase/src/ui/apps/index.ts`** and the bundle in `.../system/translations/index.ts`. ⚠️ Locate both by symbol; the card's sha `189a7322` is **not** current `main`, so re-derive rather than replay.
2. **Group headers count.** The card names nav *items*; it also says *"navigation items and group headers"* in its expected-state. Sweep for **both**, and report the count you found against the count you translated — a bundle that covers items but not headers reproduces the same mixed shell one level up.
3. ⚠️ **`check:i18n` is a convention-triggered gate that no path derivation can name** — it fires on *what the change IS* (an object-definition/bundle edit restaling bundles) and needs a **built CLI**. Determine whether it applies here and run it if so; ⛔ a skipped gate is not a passed gate, and "not in the dispatch's list" is not a clearance.

## Non-negotiables

- ⛔ **Do not translate by pattern-matching the English into Chinese one string at a time without reading the app.** These are navigation labels a user reads as a set; consistency of register across the sidebar matters more than any single string, and the existing bundle already establishes the register to match.
- **`examples/app-showcase/src/ui/apps/index.ts` is READ-ONLY here** — the fix belongs in the translation bundle, not in the source labels. If it turns out the label set cannot be keyed without touching that file, that is a surface breach: **report it, do not take it.**
- ⛔ Never `git add -A`; ⛔ never raise a ledger/baseline; ⛔ never touch `content/docs/releases/`.
- ⭐ **Capture real exit status**: `cmd > /tmp/out 2>&1; EXIT=$?` — ⛔ never `cmd | tail` then `$?` (reads tail's status, always 0). Filed as **#9552** today and adopted by two devs since. Run the gate union **after** the final commit, on the pushed tree.
- ⭐ `pull_request_read method=get_status` is a **false-green source** on this repo (returns Vercel statuses, zero check runs). Use check runs.

Related-but-distinct, per the card: #8094 / #5084 / #5407 are Console runtime chrome strings; this is the example app's own navigation metadata.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #9597. Ready-flip held pending CI convergence.

Reviewer of record: `domain:metadata` seat, round 4, session `session_017qYPmkKEsfbWY1yVg83p8F`. I read the diff and the file list **before** the terminal report arrived, so the checks below are independent of its self-description.

### Checklist

| item | reading |
|---|---|
| PR form | draft ✅ · base `main` ✅ · first line **`Fixes #9260`** ✅ |
| changed files | **2**, from `get_files`: the bundle and `scripts/i18n-coverage-baseline.json` |
| ⭐ **surface honoured** | **`examples/app-showcase/src/ui/apps/index.ts` is NOT in the diff.** I checked this myself — it was the one file the dispatch made read-only, and the temptation to "just add the label there" is exactly what the fence existed for |
| clause ② | no — example-app translation data, `private: true`, no `packages/spec/**` |
| governed fork | clean ⇒ merge queue |
| changeset | **`skip-changeset` label**, and ⭐ **existence confirmed via `get_label` before use**, applied as a read-then-write union so the bot's `size/m` survived, then read back. That is the "⛔ never mint a label that does not exist" rule executed rather than recited |

### The counts, and why they are a measurement

Nav items **49/49**, group headers **8/8**, app label **1/1** — ⭐ **and the translated id set was diffed against the id set `os lint --json` reports** (57 `i18n/missing-navigation` + 1 `i18n/missing-app`, zh-CN only): no missing ids, no extra ids. That is what makes it a count rather than an impression.

⭐ **The one discrepancy is explained rather than smoothed over**: `nav_sep_reports` is a separator that declares no label, so there is no key to translate. A report that said "49 found, 49 translated" without accounting for the 50th node would have been the weaker answer.

### ⭐ It answered a question I did not ask, and it is the one that matters

Why were **12 object entries already translated** while the sidebar stayed entirely English? Because nav labels are **their own key space** — `apps.APP.navigation.ID.label`, applied by `translateApp` at the `/meta` boundary — and **an authored nav label is kept verbatim**, so the object's translated `pluralLabel` is never consulted for the menu. ⇒ This was never "a few missing strings"; `objects.*` **structurally could not** cover it. Without that, the natural next step would have been to add more object translations and watch nothing change.

### ⭐ The reverse verification is real, and cleverer than the usual shape

`check:i18n-coverage` went **RED on this change before the baseline was updated** — *"untranslated declared strings improved 451 → 393 — ratchet DOWN"* — and green after `--update`.

That red/green pair is the proof the gate **sees** this diff. It matters here more than usual because the baseline edit is the one line in this PR that could look like gaming a gate: a bare `451 → 393` with no translations behind it is exactly the shape a ratchet exists to catch. The red proves the improvement is real and the ratchet is following it, not leading it. **Direction verified independently: down, and no other config's entry moved.**

### ⭐ The gate that did NOT apply was run anyway, with its population measured

My dispatch flagged `check:i18n` as a convention-triggered gate that no path derivation can name. The answer came back **verified, not assumed**: its population is `packages/` directories owning a `scripts/i18n-extract.config.ts`, and `find examples -name i18n-extract.config.ts` is **empty** — so it does not cover this file. It was run regardless (OK, 9 packages), and so was the nav-shaped sibling `check:app-nav-i18n` (OK), for the same reason. ⇒ "not in the dispatch's list" was not treated as a clearance, and neither was "probably doesn't apply".

### The remit sentence — the restraint I was hoping for

The header claimed a columns-only remit, which is **why nothing caught this**: the invariant was scoped narrower than the surface it reads as covering. The fix widens it by **one descriptive sentence** and ⛔ explicitly **does not** promise every declared surface is translated — it points at the baseline (still **393**) as the measure of what remains. ⭐ Widening it into a guarantee would have been the easy mistake and would have made the header false in a new way.

### Translation quality — spot readings, since no gate can judge this

- **Vocabulary is reused, not re-minted**: 项目/任务/客户/联系人/发票 from the object blocks, 任务清单 · 工时按状态分布 · 活动时间线 · 工作地点地图 from `showcase_task._views`, 分流 from `showcase_inquiry._views.triage`, 业务单元 from the platform bundle. A nav entry says the same word as the surface it opens.
- ⭐ **`nav_active_projects` reads the filter, not the name**: the page's base filter hides completed projects rather than matching `status = active`, so it says **进行中的项目** rather than 活跃. That is reading the semantics before choosing the word.
- ⭐ **`nav_expense_reports`** carries its own note that `showcase_expense_report` has no translated object label (it sits inside the frozen baseline), so the nav label stands alone deliberately.
- **`grp_auth_*`** share 页面搭建 exactly as the English shares "Authoring" — the grouping survives translation.

### Out-of-scope finding, correctly filed in the other repo

**objectui#5197** — `NavigationRenderer`'s `isCustomized` guard compares the nav label against the node's **ID**, so `resolveGroupLabel` / `resolveItemLabel` are **unreachable for every real nav entry** (a label never equals `grp_*` / `nav_*`). Harmless today because `translateApp` localizes server-side at the `/meta` boundary — ⚠️ but `navGroupLabel`'s own docstring promises exactly that unreachable path. **Another declared ≠ enforced**, filed unassigned in the repo where the fix lands, dedup searched first. ⛔ Correctly not folded in.

### ⛔ Not enqueued yet

CI was still converging at review time (21 runs, 0 red, the heavy gates `in_progress`). Flip waits on every job's own conclusion; ⛔ `get_status` is a false-green source on this repo and was not used. Flip-point re-read armed.
